senses.definition: (obsolete, intransitive) To make a short blast on a horn.

examples: His horse pooped right in the middle of the parade.
synonyms: drop the kids off at the pool
take the Browns to the Super Bowl

subsenses.definition: (informal, transitive) To defecate in or on something.
examples: You might want a spare change of underwear in case you poop your pants.
synonyms: drop the kids off at the pool
take the Browns to the Super Bowl

subsenses.definition: (informal, reflexive) To defecate on one's person.
examples: You'll poop yourself if you have to walk all five miles home without stopping.
synonyms: drop the kids off at the pool
take the Browns to the Super Bowl

examples: The dog poop is on the grass.

senses.definition: The sound of a steam engine's whistle, typically low-pitched.

quotes.text: Two minutes passed - five - seven - ten. "Poop! Poop!" Everyone knew that whistle, and a mighty cheer went up as the Queen's train glided into the station.

senses.definition: (Internet slang) Ellipsis of YouTube poop (“video mashup”).

quotes.text: The resulting video (called a “poop”) subverts its original content by slicing and dicing the video and audio, adding visual effects, and mashing several videos into one.
quotes.reference: 2012 November 3, Brad Evan Rosen, “YouTube Poop: Meme as Art, Community – by “William A – YLT2012””, in Yale Law Tech:

quotes.text: And nobody really set out to design YTP to work this way—only a fraction of YTPs ever succeed in releasing enough neurochemicals, and those are the videos that get elevated and then remixed into a new round of poops.
quotes.reference: 2020 March 3, Zack O'Malley Greenburg, “YouTube Poop And The ‘Sanic’ Boom: Digesting The Strangest Slice Of Google’s $15B Video Business”, in Forbes:

quotes.text: I don't need him for a friend. I can have fun by myself! ... Poop.

senses.definition: A set of data or general information, written or spoken, usually concerning machinery or a process.
examples: Here’s the info paper with the poop on that carburetor.

quotes.text: If Exxon has already made a find, and someone knows about it, they'd be the most likely to be directing the show. We just need to discover who has ties to the D.O.F and is close enough to Exxon to have the inside poop.

examples: I'm pooped from working so hard.

senses.definition: (reflexive) (with out) To become tired and exhausted.
examples: He pooped out a few strides from the finish line.

senses.definition: (nautical) The rear part (after end) of a ship or other vessel.
examples: For quotations using this term, see Citations:poop.

quotes.text: Omens thicken upon us […] Next, the stumbling of the King whenas he went upon the poop of the long ship which bare us on this voyage to these islands.
quotes.reference: 1922, E[ric] R[ücker] Eddison, The Worm Ouroboros: A Romance, London: Jonathan Cape […], →OCLC, page 18:

senses.definition: (transitive) To break seawater with the poop (stern) of a vessel, especially the poop deck.
(transitive) To break over the stern of (a vessel).
examples: We were pooped within hailing of the quay and were nearly sunk.

quotes.text: Another night, as we were scudding before a heavy gale of wind, and a tremendous sea rolling after us, we had the misfortune to be pooped, as the phrase is, by a wave or sea striking our stern, which stove in the cabin-windows, and rushing impetuously through the cabin, and along the main-deck, bore down all before it.
quotes.reference: 1819, James Hardy Vaux, chapter 18, in Memoirs of James Hardy Vaux, volume 1, page 207:

quotes.text: Pooping is a hazard of another nature, and is also peculiar to the process of scudding. It merely means the ship's being overtaken by waters while running from them, when the crest of a sea, broken by the resistance, is thrown inboard over the taffrail or quarter.
quotes.reference: 1838, Robert Walsh, The Museum of Foreign Literature, Science, and Art: Volume 33, page 376:

quotes.text: Aside from battles, the history of nations seemed to consist of nothing but powerless old poops like myself, heavily medicated and vaguely beloved in the long ago, coming to kiss the boots of young psychopaths.
quotes.reference: 1976, Kurt Vonnegut, chapter 48, in Slapstick, Delacorte Press, page 224:
